verdicts.why: A plan or blueprint for making something is named plainly; the word takes no side on the thing planned.
Conceiving something in the mind is a neutral act; the gloss carries no approval or suspicion, whatever the novel's scheming contexts suggest.
Compelling someone or something is a strong meaning, not an attitude; the word is the plain term for compulsion beside make or compel.
Moving something with force describes the manner of movement and passes no judgement on it.
Taking by force is an unpleasant referent in a plain word; the word reports the seizure without an attitude toward it.
Squeezing something into a tight space is purely descriptive of physical action.
Giving a speech to an audience is described neutrally; the word implies nothing about speaker or listener.
Dealing with a matter verbally or artistically is a neutral act with no built-in approval or dismissal.
Greeting someone by a prescribed form or title is a plain description of the act, without attitude toward either party.
Writing an address on an envelope is a bare practical action.
Directing a question at someone is neutral; the plain neighbour ask carries the same stance.
Locating something by address is technical vocabulary with no evaluative content.
Aiming at a golf ball before a stroke is a technical description of a physical motion.
A liking or leaning toward something is named without the speaker approving or disparaging it; the sentences show it used for both promising and doubted attachments.
A natural disposition toward a condition is a neutral tendency word, like tendency or propensity, taking no side.
A geometric angle carries no attitude.
An orbital angle in degrees is purely technical.
The dip of a magnetic needle is a measured quantity with no evaluative content.
Following a course is neutral movement or progress; the word is formal beside go on but passes no judgement.
Continuing an activity is described without any attitude toward the activity or the person continuing it.
Denying entrance or membership is a plain statement of the act; the refusal may sting but the word itself takes no side, unlike spurn or snub.
Something that eludes a solution is described figuratively but neutrally, with no attitude toward it.
Immunological rejection of tissue is medical description with no evaluative load.
Reaching harmony of opinion is named plainly; the word implies nothing about whether agreeing was wise or servile, even where the novel shows Mr. Collins agreeing to everything.
Being suitable to someone, as food or climate agrees with a person, states a fit without judging either side.
